IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p55/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p55/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p55/r11.claim: Some explain سجّيل through Persian sang and gil, meaning stone and clay.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p55/r11.anchor: ولهذا ذهب قوم في تفسير (سجيل) إلى سنك وكل. أي حجر وطين

ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n53/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n53/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:73#n53/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to his note 114 on surah 11 for this verse's explanation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.claim: At dawn or an unexpected hour, a terrible cry overtook the people; their land was ruined and stones of baked clay rained down on them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r1.anchor: Ardından ülkeleri harap oldu, üzerlerine pişmiş çamurdan oluşan taşlar yağdı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.claim: Their fate illustrates what befalls a people who defy God, disregard a prophet’s warnings and moral values, and persist shamelessly in disgraceful immorality.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:15:73/r2.anchor: Allah’a âsi olup peygamberin ikazlarını ciddiye almadan, hiçbir değer yargısı tanımadan, yüz kızartıcı ahlâksızlıkları bile hayasızca ve fütursuzca işlemekte ısrar eden bir toplumun âkıbeti ortaya konmuştur

BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r1.claim: The town was lifted close to heaven on Gabriel’s wing and then overturned upon its people, leaving it inverted.
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r1.anchor: بأن رفعناها إلى قريب من السماء على جناح جبريل ثم قلبناها عليهم

BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r2.claim: In the grammar, “its upper part” is the first object of “We made” and “its lower part” the second; this order intensifies the horror compared with the reverse.
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r2.anchor: وقوله عاليها مفعول أول لجعلنا وسافلها مفعول ثان له وهو أدخل في الهول والفظاعة

BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r3.claim: The stones rained down during the upheaval before the town’s inversion was complete.
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r3.anchor: وأمطرنا عليهم في تضاعيف ذلك قبل تمام الانقلاب

BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r4.claim: Al-Qamus defines sijjil as clodlike stones or a Persian-derived term; other explanations say the stones were baked in Hell, inscribed with the people’s names, or came from the decree recording their punishment, equating sijjil with sijjin.
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r4.anchor: قال في القاموس السجيل كسكيت حجارة كالمدر معرب (سنك كل) أو كان طبخت بنار جهنم

BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r5.speaker: الأزهري
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r5.claim: Al-Azhari calls the explanation of sijjil as sijjin, a record of punishment, the clearest of the reported definitions.
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r5.anchor: قال الأزهري هذا أحسن ما مر عندي وأبينها

BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r6.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r6.claim: Al-Kawashi says the stones also fell on those who were away from the affected lands.
BURSEVI:v4p319#2/r6.anchor: وفي "الكواشي" : وأمطرنا على شذاذهم ، أي : على من غاب عن تلك البلاد.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Lot account is historical evidence for the Quraysh, who passed the settlement; those wishing to see angels should prepare for the same fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if they desire to see angels, then they should also get ready to meet the fate of the people of Lot

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi says the verse concisely refers to the punishment's nature and introduces Farāhī's detailed account of it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This verse rather concisely refers to the nature of punishment that came to them. My mentor, ustāz Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī, has explained

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Farāhī describes a sand-laden wind forming clay stones, pelting Lot's people, then intensifying until their houses were overturned and buried by sand and pebbles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: My mentor, ustāz Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī, has explained in detail its nature in his exegesis of Sūrah Dhāriyāt.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi directs readers to Farāhī's al-Fīl commentary for his research on the word sijjīl.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: is presented by him in his exegesis of Sūrah al-Fīl thus:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The author relays Farāhī's etymology of sijjīl as Persian sang, stone, plus gil, clay; the Qur'an explains it through pebbles of sijjīl and clay stones.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: is Arabicized form of two Persian words sang (stone) and gil (clay).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r15.claim: The pronoun in عاليها سافلها refers to the previously mentioned city.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r15.anchor: والضمير في عاليها سافلها عائد على المدينة المتقدمة الذكر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says it refers to the towns of Lot, although the word towns had not appeared earlier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r16.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لقرى قوم لوط، ولم يتقدم لفظ القرى.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r1.claim: “Its upper part” most naturally refers to the city, though it can refer to the towns even though they were not previously mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r1.anchor: عاليها أي المدينة كما هو الظاهر وجوز رجوعه إلى القرى وإن لم يسبق ذكرها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r2.claim: The city’s surface and what lies on it is the first object of jaʿala, and its lower part is the second.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بعاليها وجه الأرض وما عليه وهو المفعول الأول لجعل و ( سافلها ( الثاني له

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r3.claim: Stones of sijjīl were rained upon them amid the overturning.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r3.anchor: وأمطرنا عليهم ( في تضاعيف ذلك ( حجارة ( كائنة ( من سجيل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r4.claim: Sijjīl is commonly understood as hardened clay, and the word is usually considered a loan from Persian sang-gil.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r4.anchor: من طين متحجر وهو في المشهور معرب سنك كل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayd and others consider sijjīl an Arabic word and cite a variant sijjīn with nūn, supported by a line of Tamīm ibn Muqbil.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r5.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيد وطائفة إلى أنه عربي وأنه يقال فيه ( سجين ) بالنون واجتجوا بقول تميم من مقبل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r6.claim: The author regards that linguistic argument as weak.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r7.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī declined to explain the line’s word because he remembered hearing it as sakhināʾ, “hot,” rather than sajīnan.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r7.anchor: وسئل الأصمعي عن معناه في البيت فقال : لا أفسره إذ كنت أسمع وأنا حدث سخينا بالخاء المعجمة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r8.claim: Another derivation links the word to sijill, a book: the clay bore their names or God’s decree of punishment written on it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : مأخوذ من السجل وهو الكتاب أي من طين كتب عليه أسماؤهم أو كتب الله تعذيبهم به

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r1.claim: The high part of the city or villages was made their low part, turning the place upside down.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r1.anchor: عالي المدينة أو عالي قراهم. { سافلها } وصارت منقلبة بهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r2.claim: Sijjīl means hardened clay, or clay bearing writing from the word sijill; fuller explanation of the story appeared in Sūrat Hūd.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:74/r2.anchor: من طين متحجر أو طين عليه كتاب من السجل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.claim: The cry may have come at sunrise as their end, while uprooting the cities at dawn began the destruction; the city tops were turned below and stones rained on their inhabitants, unlike the pronoun reference in Hud.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r3.anchor: أعاد الضمير على المعذبين لا على مدنهم - كما مضى في سورة هود عليه السلام - لأن هذا أصرح

DURR-FULL:v5p90/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r6.claim: The destruction is a recognizable sign, like a seal-ring sent to a household that lets them recognize a genuine message.
DURR-FULL:v5p90/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إن في ذلك لآيات} قال: علامة أما ترى الرجل يرسل بخاتمه إلى أهله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r8.claim: The two pronouns in ‘its top and bottom’ refer to the city, while ‘upon them’ resumes the earlier plural group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p68/r8.anchor: وضميرا { عاليها سافلها } للمدينة . وضمير { عليهم } عائد إلى ما عادت عليه ضمائر الجمع قبله .

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409#2/r1.claim: The author refers readers to his explanation of this verse at 11:82.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p409#2/r1.anchor: قد فسرنا الآية في سورة ( هود 82 )

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p543/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p543/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p543/r2.claim: Their towns were lifted high into the sky, overturned, and pelted with stones of sijjil; Ibn Kathir refers readers to his earlier discussion of sijjil in Hud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p543/r2.anchor: وذلك مع رفع (1) بلادهم إلى عنان السماء ثم قلبها، وجعل عاليها سافلها

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.claim: The verses show that Lot's people were destroyed and the believing members of his household were saved.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8.anchor: تدل الآية على إهلاك قوم لوط ونجاة من آمن من أهله

JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.claim: The remains endure so people can learn from them, and they provide divine لطف for us.
JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10.anchor: وتدل على أن آثارها باقية ليعتبر بها، وأن فيها لطف لنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r17.claim: The stones of sijjīl are clay bearing an inscription, as supported by the description of marked stones from clay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r17.anchor: قيل : من طين ، عليه كتاب من السجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r19.claim: The pronoun in “its upper part became its lower” refers to the towns of Lot's people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p547/r19.anchor: والضمير في { عاليها سافلها } لقرى قوم لوط

MUQATIL:15:74-77/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r1.claim: God overturned the four cities and rained clay-mixed stones on Sodom, Damura, Amura, and Sabura and people outside the towns; a stone could reach someone elsewhere and kill him.
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r1.anchor: { فجعلنا } المدائن الأربع { عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليهم } سدوم، ودامورا، وعامورا وصابورا، وأمطرنا على من كان خارجا

MUQATIL:15:74-77/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r2.claim: Sijjil means stones mixed with clay.
MUQATIL:15:74-77/r2.anchor: { من سجيل } ، يعني الحجارة خلطها الطين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r1.claim: Gabriel lifted the towns of Lot’s people to heaven and then overturned them; the pronoun refers to those towns.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r1.anchor: رفعها جبريل عليه السلام إلى السماء ثم قلبها والضمير لقرى قوم لوط

NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p246/r2.claim: Stones of sijjīl were rained upon them.

RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r4.claim: God punished them in three ways: a terrible cry, overturning the city, and raining down stones of sijjīl; Rāzī says the latter details were explained in Sūrat Hūd.
RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r4.anchor: عذبهم بثلاثة أنواع من العذاب : أحدها : الصيحة الهائلة المنكرة . وثانيها : أنه جعل عاليها سافلها

STUDYQURAN:15:73/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:73/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:73/r1.claim: The account of Lot’s people here is tied to the commentary on 11:82–83.

SAMIN-DURR:15:74/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:74/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:15:74/r1.claim: The pronoun in عاليها سافلها refers to the city, whose antecedent was expressly mentioned.

SAMIN-DURR:15:74/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:15:74/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:15:74/r2.claim: He takes the pronoun to refer to the towns of Lot.

TAB-FULL:v14p94/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p94/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p94/r1.claim: Al-Tabari presents the stones of baked clay as part of the punishment of Lot’s people.
TAB-FULL:v14p94/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، عن عكرمة: {وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل} [الحجر: 74] أي من طين

TAB-FULL:v14p94/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p94/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v14p94/r2.claim: ʿIkrima explains the stones of sijjil as clay, in a report transmitted from Qatada.
TAB-FULL:v14p94/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، عن عكرمة: {وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل} [الحجر: 74] أي من طين

ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r1.claim: Sijjīl means clay bearing a written mark, deriving from sijill; the verse about stones of clay marked by God supports this reading.
ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r1.anchor: من طين عليه كتاب. واشتقاق ذلك من السجل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p637/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p637/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p637/r1.claim: The explanation of the overturning and stone rain is given in the commentary on Hūd, verse 82.

BURHAN:v4p130/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p130/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p130/r4.claim: Examples make the source and destination of transformation explicit; in “day a livelihood,” maʿāsh may mean a time noun or a verbal noun meaning livelihood.
BURHAN:v4p130/r4.anchor: في قوله ﴿ وجعلنا النهار معاشا ﴾ 15 اسم زمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.claim: The punishment in al-Hijr is harsher: the cry at sunrise, overturning of the city, and stones of baked clay exceed the rain punishment mentioned in al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p914/r3.anchor: لوجدنا أن العقوبة في سورة الحجر أشدّ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r8.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r8.claim: A report says Gabriel uprooted the city, raised it until heaven’s angels heard its roosters and dogs, then overturned it; survivors were struck by stones of baked clay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r8.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام اقتلع المدينة بجناحيه ورفعها حتى سمعت ملائكة السماء صراخ الديكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r9.claim: Sijjil is said to be a worldly term or Persian for baked-clay stones like bricks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r9.anchor: وسجيل اسم من الدنيا، وقيل لفظة فارسية، وهي الحجارة المطبوخة من الطين كالآجر
